general_information.Description: Main objectives: 'As a course within the Media and Communication curriculum, the Capstone Project is comprehensive, allowing students to apply the combined knowledge acquired from earlier courses and projects to the production of more fully-realized work. The main objectives of the course are to: - Exhibit an advanced understanding of the relationship between media and communication; - Exhibit an advanced understanding of the theories of humanities and social science; - Create a self-project as a media and communication professional; - Develop personal/ team work on a professional level of quality; - Construct professional media and communication practices; - Demonstrate proficiency in communication, presentation, and the necessary skills for professional practice, such as the capacity to organise and manage projects as well as collaborate effectively with others. This competency requires knowledge of organisational structures and work patterns in the fields of economics, media, and communication. Description: - This course requires real-work projects completed by a group of 3-5 students, each student must defend their contribution to the group project individually in front of a professional committee/examination board. - Students are strongly encouraged to form groups and actively seek their supervisor(s), who will provide the necessary guidance as they develop their projects from initial concepts or ideas to completion. - By the completion, students are expected to acquire a comprehensive understanding and skills in the field of media and communication. The project consists of four (04) main phases: (1) Research and development, (2) Pre-implementation/Pre-production, (3) Implementation/production, (4) Post-implementation/post-production, distribution (if applicable), and evaluation Students are required to participate in and deliver progress reports to the department's professional committee at the CP Proposal completion stage. Students are expected to demonstrate a high level of professionalism when discussing, organising, presenting, and critiquing their work, as well as when implementing research strategies that contribute to the completion of the project in response to constructive feedback from supervisor(s) and professional committees. Completion Criteria: - Progress on Project (04 reports): 40% - Final report/Production Book: 10% - Project Defense: 50% Overall Final Project Mark: 100% Mark of each report must be >= 4/10 Final Report/Production Book >= 4/10 Oral Project Defense >= 5/10 Final Report/Production Book must be submitted before deadline
general_information.StudentTasks: (1) read and understand rightly all relevant documents for the CPs published on FLM (such as guidelines, requirements, and regulations, etc.); (2) Participate in the Orientation meeting conducted by the Department (3) Choose topics for Capstone Projects so that the topics fall within the concentrations, and fully meet the requirements of common research ethics, law, fine customs and traditional values in Vietnam; an approval from supervisor(s) and the University may be required. (3) Divide and schedule work for each member of group approximatelly based on supervisor(s)' advise and the CP Guidelines and Syllabus; (4) Students are required to attend at least 80% of scheduled meetings with their supervisor(s) to be eligible for the thesis or capstone defense; (5) Conduct research, produce documents and media products, and write reports (in English) according to the CPs requirements from the University and the Department; preference the Guideline for details. (6) Avoiding Plagiarism and Copyright Infringement in all reports and media productions; (7) Defense individually the CPs in front of examination Committees according to the requirements and regulations of the University and the Department.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Formulate, scope, and contextualise project concepts within the context of relevant media and communication expertise
Develop a research plan with the potential to yield results that can inform strategic or planning decisions.
Perform effective research, data analysis, and interpretation of the results.
Generate a strategy/ plan based on the research findings, a high level of critical thinking, and a comprehensive knowledge of media and communication.
Deliver plans with effective media productions, the utmost proficiency of risk management expertise, and the capability to simultaneously evaluate the plan.
Produce academically satisfactory reports exemplifying professional competence in the field of media and communication.
Conduct a project professionally and ethically, including the ethical use or adoption of AI-assisted tools, while working harmoniously with group members.
Present and defend the project in front of examiner boards with professionalism.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Combination of all relevant acquired knowledge, and research and written skills
assessments.Grading Guide: • A Production Book/ Final report accounting for 10% of the whole project must include 04 reports clarified in The Student’s Guide. Based on the syllabus schedule, the Final report/ Production Book will be evaluated by the supervisor(s). It will be one of the resources for Professional Committees to evaluate the content of the whole project at an oral defence. • Individual mark is decided by the supervisor(s) and is assessed based on the actual contribution by that individual to the report. The individual mark can be lower or higher than the group mark.
assessments.Note: The capstone paper should not exceed 150 pages excluding Tables of content, lists of figures/ tables/ bibliography, and appendices, unless otherwise agreed upon with the supervisor(s)

assessments.CLO: CLO1, CLO2, CLO3, CLO4, CLO5, CLO6,CLO7
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: • Report No.1: Introduction, Research & Development, • Report No.2: Pre – Production • Report No.3: Production/Implementation & Distribution • Report No.4: Post – production, Evaluation and Reflection
assessments.Grading Guide: • Based on the schedule of the syllabus, each group report will be evaluated by supervisor(s). This evaluation is called progress assessment. • Individual mark for each progress assessment report is decided by the group supervisor and is assessed on the basis of the actual contribution by that individual to the group project. The individual mark can be lower or higher than the group mark and is in the range from 0% to 120% of the group mark where the average score of group members cannot be more than group mark.
assessments.Note: All four progress assessment reports account for 40% of the whole project with weights: - Report 1: 10% - Report 2: 10% - Report 3: 10% - Report 4: 10%

assessments.CLO: CLO1,CLO2,CLO3, CLO4, CLO5, CLO6, CLO7, CLO8
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Combination of all relevant acquired knowledge, and practice and presentation skills
assessments.Grading Guide: • Presentation mark is given by each member of the professional committee for each student on the final project presentation. This personal mark is the average of all members of the professional committee. The Professional Committee of the Oral Defense needs to submit the Production Book cold grading scores before the Oral Defense session.Total presentation time for each group is 50 mins. Each student must make his or her own presentation
assessments.Note: 50% of the whole project including: - Project Content: 30% - Presentation: 20%
